analysis.note: Causal particle here, glossed by yasmāt.
Ātmanepada intransitive: “becomes firmly established”; Śaṅkara explains it as becoming immovable in Self-nature.

justifications.decision: The locative is taken as the circumstance in which the result arises; Śaṅkara frames the verse as praise of prasannatā, serenity, and glosses the related prasanna-cetasaḥ by a well-composed inner organ.
justifications.chosen: prasāde = in/when there is mental serenity (prasāda), not divine favor or mere stylistic clarity.

evidence.translation: Of one whose mind is serene, whose inner instrument is well-composed.

justifications.decision: The compound is read as “all sorrows,” not “sorrows of all [people/things].” Śaṅkara glosses the genitive plural with ādhyātmikādīnām.
options_considered: all sorrows, i.e. the ādhyātmika and other kinds
justifications.chosen: sarva-duḥkhānām = of all sorrows, specifically including the ādhyātmika and other classes.

evidence.translation: Of all sorrows, beginning with the internal/psychophysical ones.

justifications.decision: Although hāni can mean decrease, Śaṅkara explicitly glosses it by vināśa, destruction.
justifications.chosen: hāniḥ = destruction/cessation, not mere loss or diminution.

justifications.decision: The pronoun is not left as a vague “of this”; Śaṅkara supplies yateḥ as its referent.
justifications.chosen: asya = of this yati, this disciplined ascetic/practitioner.

justifications.decision: The form could be read superficially as “of a serene mind,” but Śaṅkara treats it as qualifying the person: svasthāntaḥ-karaṇasya, and then speaks of the prasanna-cetas as having an established buddhi.
options_considered: bahuvrīhi: of the person whose mind is serene
karmadhāraya/substantive: of the serene mind itself
justifications.chosen: prasanna-cetasaḥ = of the serene-minded person, one whose inner organ is composed.

evidence.translation: Of one whose mind is serene, whose inner instrument is well-composed.
Thus, for the serene-minded one, the intellect is established.

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara glosses hi by yasmāt and āśu by śīghram, so the second hemistich explains the first rather than merely adding emphasis.
justifications.chosen: hi is causal, “for/because,” and āśu is adverbial, “quickly.”

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara expands the verb as complete, all-around abiding and then states the intended sense as niścalībhavati, becoming motionless, with ātma-svarūpa. The translation therefore uses “becomes firmly established,” not merely “stands” or “pervades.”
justifications.chosen: buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate = the intellect quickly becomes firmly established, immovable as Self-nature itself.

evidence.quote: buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate ākāśam iva pari samantāt avatiṣṭhate, ātma-svarūpeṇaiva niścalībhavatīty arthaḥ
evidence.translation: The intellect becomes established; it abides all around, as it were like space; the meaning is that it becomes motionless as Self-nature itself.

translation:
When serenity (prasāda) is present, the destruction of all sorrows arises for this yati.
For, in the serene-minded one, the intellect (buddhi) quickly becomes firmly established, immovable as Self-nature itself.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might render prasāda as “favor” or generic “clarity”; Śaṅkara treats it as mental serenity, prasannatā, of the inner organ.
It might translate hāni as mere “loss” or “diminution”; Śaṅkara requires vināśa, destruction/cessation.
It might leave asya as a vague “of this”; Śaṅkara identifies the referent as the yati.
It might take prasanna-cetasaḥ as “of the serene mind” rather than “of the serene-minded person”; Śaṅkara’s svasthāntaḥ-karaṇasya supports the bahuvrīhi reading.
It might flatten paryavatiṣṭhate to “settles down”; Śaṅkara adds the force of complete, immovable establishment in Self-nature.

upajāyate: ByT5 gave the prefixed lemma upajan; per the requested format I give the bare root jan with prefix upa. The verb is Kartari, intransitive, not passive.

prasanna-cetasaḥ: ByT5 split prasanna and cetasaḥ and tagged cetas as a separate genitive; I analyze prasannacetas as a masculine genitive singular bahuvrīhi, following Śaṅkara’s svasthāntaḥ-karaṇasya. The verifier’s tool_error/unsupported-relation report is noted but does not overturn the analysis.
paryavatiṣṭhate: ByT5 gave prefixed lemma paryavasthā; per the requested format I give the bare root sthā with prefixes pari and ava.

kiṃ ca - prasanna-cetasaḥ svasthāntaḥ-karaṇasya hi yasmāt āśu śīghraṃ buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate ākāśam iva pari samantāt avatiṣṭhate, ātma-svarūpeṇaiva niścalībhavatīty arthaḥ |
